text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Emperor of France from 1804 to 1815, NAPOLEON BONAPARTE, was born in 1769.
Sir WALTER SCOTT, Scott, Scottish author, was born in 1771.
He wrote many historical romances including "Guy Mannering",
"Ivanhoe" and "Heart of Midlothian".
Scottish/Australian journalist JOSEPH MELVIN was born in
1852. He reported, via telegraph, from the NED KELLY siege at
Glenrowan.
Founder of the British Labour Party JAMES KEIR HARDIE was
born in 1856.
American actress ETHEL BARRYMORE was born in 1879.
English soldier and writer T.E. (THOMAS EDWARD) LAWRENCE,
who was known as Lawrence Of Arabia, was born in 1888.
English playwright ROBERT BOLT, who wrote "A Man For All
Seasons", was born in 1924.
Canadian jazz pianist and composer OSCAR PETERSEN was born
The British Princess Royal, ANNE, was born in 1950.
American singer with the Beastie Boys, MCA (ADAM YAUCH) was born in 1967.
**EVENTS**
1057 : MACBETH, King of Scotland whose life was the basis
for Shakespeare's play, was killed by MALCOLM CANMORE at Lumphanan, near Aberdeen.
1534 : The Society of Jesus (Jesuits) was founded in
Paris by St IGNATIUS of Loyola.
1820 : In New South Wales, traffic control was introduced
with the rule that all horse-drawn vehicles must Keep Left.
1834 : British parliament passed an act allowing for the
colonisation of South Australia.
1903 : The first Rugby test between Australia and New
Zealand was played at the Sydney Cricket Ground. New Zealand won 22 to 3.
1914 : The 82 km Panama Canal was opened, connecting the
Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
1922 : A concert by DAME NELLIE MELBA in Geelong raised
more than seven thousand pounds for the Kitchener Memorial hospital.
1944 : U.S. Seventh Army began Operation Dragoon, a
landing on the French Riviera to open up a second front after the Normandy landings of June.
1945 : World War II ended with the surrender of Japan.
During the six years, Australia lost almost 34,000 soldiers and a further 180,000 were wounded.
1947 : The Indian Independence Bill came into force,
setting up the two independent states of India and Pakistan.
1949 : Australia's Prime Minister BEN CHIFLEY called in
the troops to work in NSW open-cut coal mines, in an attempt to break a strike which closed the mines for almost seven weeks.
1965 : A Beatles concert attracted 56,000 fans to Shea
Stadium in New York, creating a new outdoor audience record for a pop concert.
1969 : The three-day Woodstock Music and Art Fair opened
at Bethel in upstate New York. The outdoor rock concert attracted more than 300,000 people and leading performers.
1975 : The President of Bangladesh, Sheikh MUJIBUR
RAHMAN, was killed by army officers in a dawn coup which overthrew his government.
1979 : Two Soviet Aeroflot airliners collided in mid-air
over Ukraine, killing 173.
1994 : Sudanese security agents, tipped off by Paris,
captured wanted international guerrilla ILLICH RAMIREZ SANCHEZ, known as "Carlos the Jackal".
1995 : Fifty years after World War Two ended in the
Pacific, Japan made its first clear-cut apology for the country's wartime actions.
1996 : Senior Bosnian officials signed an agreement to
fully form the country's Moslem-Croat Federation and dismantle the self-styled Bosnian Croat republic of Herceg-Bosna.
